input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 sits at or above our preferred position and is favourable to us. 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets without Vendor's consent (notice only, and "Affiliate" is defined at 1.1 by >50% control). 24.2 bars Vendor from assigning, delegating material performance, or transferring by change of control without our prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, so the walk-away trigger is absent. 24.3 does not undercut 24.1: it applies only "For other assignments" (i.e., those outside the 24.1/24.2 carve-outs) and imposes a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard; 13.3 reinforces our ability to transfer licence rights on a permitted assignment. The only wording short of the ideal preferred formulation is that the competitor bar is limited to a "direct" competitor and is expressed as subject to our own consent — a minor sub-element noted here rather than redlined, since Vendor assignment already requires our consent in all cases. No redline proposed.
